'''Manfred Theodor Reetz''' (13 August 1943 – 23 April 2026) was a German chemist and professor of [[organic chemistry]], who served as director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Coal Research]] from 1991 until 2011. His research focused on [[directed evolution]], [[enzymes]] in organic chemistry, and [[stereoselective]] [[biocatalysis]].<ref name="Reetz75">{{cite web| title=75th Birthday: Manfred T. Reetz| website=ChemistryViews| date=13 August 2018| url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/11086808/75th_Birthday_Manfred_T__Reetz.html| access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Reetz was born in [[Jelenia Góra|Hirschberg]], [[Gau Lower Silesia]] on 13 August 1943, and immigrated to the US in 1952.<ref name="CV">{{cite web | title=Organische Synthese | trans-title=Organic Synthesis | website=Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung | date=17 February 2012 | url=http://www.kofo.mpg.de/de/forschung/organische-synthese | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120217033157/http://www.kofo.mpg.de/de/forschung/organische-synthese | archive-date=17 February 2012 | url-status=dead | language=de | access-date=5 November 2018 }}</ref><ref name="Hahn"/> After studying chemistry at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] and the [[University of Michigan]], he returned to Germany to obtain his Ph.D. under [[Ulrich Schöllkopf]] at the [[University of Göttingen]]. He subsequently worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Marburg]] where he completed his habilitation in 1978. After two years at the [[University of Bonn]], he returned to Marburg as full professor in 1980. In 1991 he was appointed director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Coal Research]] in [[Mülheim]], a position that he held until 2011.<ref name="CV"/><ref name="Reetz75"/>

Reetz died on 23 April 2026, at the age of 82.<ref>Frank Neese: [https://www.kofo.mpg.de/obituary-reetz "The Max-Planck-Institut für Kohlenforschung (Fundation under Private Law) Mourns the Loss of its Long-Standing Director Prof. Dr. Dr. h. c. Manfred T. REETZ"]. ''kofo.mpg.de'', 4 May 2026. Retrieved 5 May 2026.</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Among the awards that Reetz received are the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize|Leibniz Prize]] (1989),<ref name="CV"/> the Nagoya Gold Medal Award of Organic Chemistry (2000),<ref name="CV"/> the [[Royal Society of Chemistry|RSC]] [[Centenary Prize]] (2002),<ref name="RSC">{{cite web|title=RSC Centenary Prizes|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/CentenaryPrizes/ |publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]|access-date=5 November 2018|language=en}}</ref> the {{ill|Karl Ziegler Prize|de|Karl-Ziegler-Preis}} (2005),<ref name="Ziegler">{{cite web | title=Karl-Ziegler-Stiftung | trans-title=Karl Ziegler Foundation | website=Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker e.V. | url=https://www.gdch.de/gdch/stiftungen/ziegler-stiftung.html | language=de | access-date=5 November 2018 | archive-date=4 November 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104215006/https://www.gdch.de/gdch/stiftungen/ziegler-stiftung.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> the {{ill|Prelog Medal|de|Prelog-Medaille und -Vorlesung}} (2006),<ref name="Prelog">{{cite web | title=Frühere Prelog-Lektoren und deren Laudatien | trans-title=Previous Prelog Lecturers | website=ETH Zürich | date=13 March 2018 | url=https://www.chab.ethz.ch/forschung/institute-und-laboratorien/LOC/prelog-vorlesung/fruehere-prelog-lektoren.html | access-date=5 November 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904011224/https://www.chab.ethz.ch/forschung/institute-und-laboratorien/LOC/prelog-vorlesung/fruehere-prelog-lektoren.html | archive-date=4 September 2017 | url-status=dead }}</ref> the [[American Chemical Society|ACS]] [[Arthur C. Cope Award]] (2009),<ref name="Cope">{{cite web | title=Arthur C. Cope Award | website=American Chemical Society | url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/arthur-c-cope-award.html | access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref> the [[Tetrahedron Prize]] (2011),<ref name="Tetrahedron">{{cite journal | last=Taylor | first=Richard J.K. | title=The 2011 Tetrahedron prize for creativity in organic chemistry | journal=Tetrahedron | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=68 | issue=37 | year=2012 | issn=0040-4020 | doi=10.1016/j.tet.2012.07.050 | page=7529}}</ref> the [[Otto Hahn Prize]] (2011),<ref name="Hahn">{{cite web | title=M. Reetz Receives Otto Hahn Prize | website=ChemistryViews | date=22 November 2011 | url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/1076753/M__Reetz_Receives_Otto_Hahn_Prize.html | access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref> and the International Kyoto Conference on New Aspects of Organic Chemistry (IKCOC) Prize (2012).<ref name="IKCOC">{{cite web | title=M. Reetz Wins IKCOC Prize | website=ChemistryViews | date=12 November 2012 | url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/2101755/M__Reetz_Wins_IKCOC_Prize.html | access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref> He was elected to the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] in 1997.<ref name="Leopoldina">{{cite web| title=Mitgliederverzeichnis - Prof. Dr. Manfred T. Reetz| trans-title=Member Directory - Prof. Manfred T. Reetz| website=Leopoldina | date=4 June 2018| url=https://www.leopoldina.org/de/mitglieder/mitgliederverzeichnis/member/613/| language=de| access-date=4 November 2018}}</ref> He was elected a foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/6712 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200426075129/https://knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/6712 |title=Manfred Reetz |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=26 April 2020}}</ref>
